clue.text: Make mess, having died in control centre

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for died within the control centre word

parts.note: a war room is the command centre from which a campaign is directed
D is the standard abbreviation for died in genealogies and records

explanation.surface: Someone causes chaos after a death in the operations room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make mess' reads as causing chaos, but 'Make' is a link and 'mess' is the noun: the officers' dining room on a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardroom is the officers' mess on a naval vessel, where they eat and relax.

clue.text: A trickster shortly takes in German Land

indicators.note: takes in means the trimmed trickster word holds the German abbreviation
shortly means the trickster word is cut short at its end

parts.note: a liar is a deceiver or trickster

explanation.surface: A con artist briefly visits a German state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims LIAR to LIA, which 'takes in' GER. 'Land' looks like a German Land (state), but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a country, a land in North Africa.

clue.text: One way to write two hundred sheets — that's fat and thick

parts.words: One way to write two hundred
parts.note: CC is two hundred in Roman numerals, a double C
a ream is a quantity of paper sheets

explanation.surface: Writing a large number on a stack of paper, which is a fat and thick task.
explanation.definitionFit: Double cream is a rich, thick cream with a high fat content.

clue.text: Publication with nothing left to pass on

parts.note: O, the zero, means nothing
to pass on is a euphemism for to die

explanation.surface: A magazine with nothing left before it folds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oldie is a British magazine aimed at older readers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oldie is a British monthly magazine, so a publication.

clue.text: Good book from a beat-up character

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for beat is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
chi is a character of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Bible taken from a battered fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LAM to MAL in this down clue; 'Good book' is a crossword term for the Bible, here one book of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Malachi is the last book of the Old Testament, a book of the Good Book.

clue.text: Almost be unable to see nasty little thing

indicators.note: almost means the phrase stops one letter short of its full length

parts.note: to go blind is to become unable to see

explanation.surface: Something small and horrid is nearly blinding you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter D from GO BLIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblin is a mischievous, ugly little creature of folklore.

clue.text: In charity performance, opera needs giant sort of tortoise

parts.note: a gala is a festive show, often for charity
Pag is the usual nickname for Leoncavallo's opera Pagliacci, as in the double bill Cav and Pag
OS, outsize, is the clothing abbreviation for a giant size

explanation.surface: A huge tortoise is needed for an opera staged at a charity gala.
explanation.walkthrough: Opera lovers call the double bill of Cavalleria Rusticana and Pagliacci 'Cav and Pag', so PAG is an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The Galapagos giant tortoise is a species named after the Pacific islands where it lives.

clue.text: Take a knock in flutter

definitions.meaning: to have an innings at cricket, a knock being an informal word for an innings
to blink or flicker, as of eyelids

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter's innings is called a knock.
explanation.definitionFit: Bat means both to take one's turn batting at cricket and to flutter the eyelashes.

clue.text: It helps asthmatic get home less unwell

parts.note: in means at home
haler means healthier, the comparative of hale

explanation.surface: An asthma sufferer recovers at home.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler is the device asthmatics use to breathe in medication.

clue.text: Farmer's daughter's desire to follow sad youth back to class

indicators.note: to follow puts the desire word after everything before it

parts.note: sad means glum

indicators.note: back says the word for youth is read in reverse

parts.note: a youth is a lad
CL is an abbreviation for class
an itch is a craving or desire

explanation.surface: A rural girl longs to follow a gloomy boy back to school.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is Gulliver's nurse in Brobdingnag, in Swift's Gulliver's Travels; 'back' turns the youth word around, and CL is the dictionary abbreviation for class.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gulliver's Travels the giant farmer's daughter who cares for Gulliver is named Glumdalclitch.

clue.text: It affords ventilation in restaurant, say

indicators.note: say signals that the restaurant word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a grill is a restaurant serving ... food

explanation.surface: A vent in a restaurant lets the air circulate.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is a grating of bars that lets air pass through an opening.

clue.text: Stockholm and Santiago are and have

definitions.text: Stockholm and Santiago are and have

parts.words: Stockholm and Santiago are and have
parts.note: the two cities are seats of national government, and each name also begins with an upper-case S

explanation.surface: A puzzling statement about two foreign cities.
explanation.walkthrough: Stockholm and Santiago are capital cities, and they have capital letters at the start: the same word in two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitals means both chief cities of countries and upper-case letters, and these names are both.

clue.text: Great buildings where traitors were executed

definitions.meaning: the chopping blocks at the Tower of London, where traitors were beheaded

explanation.walkthrough: The Tower of London was a place of execution, with beheadings on the block.
explanation.definitionFit: Tower blocks are tall residential buildings, and the Tower's blocks were used for beheadings.

clue.text: "Tom here!" (jeers)

definitions.meaning: a tomcat announcing itself, read as a feline call
derisive shouts and whistles of disapproval

explanation.walkthrough: A tom is a male cat, so 'Tom here!' is a cat calling out.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisive whistling and shouting at someone is known as catcalling, which also fits a cat's call.

clue.text: A healthy one could get Lesley fit

indicators.note: could get suggests the name and adjective can be turned into something new

explanation.surface: Following a healthy way of living could make Lesley fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could get' rearranges LESLEY FIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A healthy lifestyle is a way of living; the definition reads 'a healthy one' as 'a healthy way of living'.

clue.text: Diet here restricted; it's contemptible

indicators.note: restricted means the town's name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: the Diet of Worms was the 1521 imperial assembly held in the German city of Worms

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a meagre diet served here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' is not food but an assembly: the Diet of Worms tried Martin Luther. 'restricted' cuts the final S from WORMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A worm is a contemptible, spineless person.

clue.text: Old woman's home with spades to work in garden

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
to hoe is to dig and weed garden soil

explanation.surface: An elderly woman's house comes with spades for the gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme, there was an old woman who lived in a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme old woman famously lived in a shoe with her many children.

clue.text: Most advanced pupil: he has a sick body

indicators.note: sick suggests the letters are disordered or unwell

explanation.surface: The top pupil has fallen ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' rearranges A BODY; HE stays as written at the front, with 'has' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The head boy is the senior pupil chosen to lead a British school.

clue.text: In working life, waiter needs a computer

indicators.note: working signals the letters of life are set to work in a new order

parts.note: a waiter is a server at table

explanation.surface: In their working life, a waiter needs a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges LIFE into FILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A file server is a computer that stores files for others on a network.

clue.text: Milan guide a bit lacking in energy

indicators.note: a bit means only a piece of the city and guide words is wanted

explanation.surface: A tour guide in Milan is short of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Languid means listless, slow and lacking vigour.

clue.text: Nasty look from our moth er across one grassy field

indicators.note: across means the mother figure stretches around the other pieces

parts.note: Eve is the mother of humankind in Genesis
I is the Roman numeral one
a ley is a field under grass

explanation.surface: Mother glares across a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: The page splits 'mother' over a line break; 'our mother' is the biblical first woman, mother of us all.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a malicious stare believed to cast a curse.

clue.text: Second in two averages that's grated

parts.note: par is a standard or average level

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for second within one of the averages

parts.note: the mean is an arithmetic average

explanation.surface: Two middling things come second to something shredded.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash is just punctuation; 'two averages' supplies two different words for average, the second holding the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese usually grated over food.

clue.text: Stop pensioners strike-breaking

indicators.note: breaking means the pensioners word splits the strike word apart

parts.note: to strike is to hit
the old means pensioners collectively

explanation.surface: Retirees cross a picket line and are told to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike-breaking' looks like crossing a picket line, but strike means HIT, broken open by OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Hold it is an exclamation meaning stop or wait.

clue.text: Bedding material in transport on motorway

parts.note: to haul is to transport goods
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A lorry carries bedding on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Haulm is the stalks of crops such as peas or potatoes, used as litter for bedding animals.

clue.text: Rob one of the family? No problem

definitions.meaning: Rob, or Robert, as a relative: this Robert is your father's brother
an exclamation meaning there it is, easy as that

explanation.walkthrough: Rob is short for Robert, also known as Bob, so Rob as a relative is Bob being your uncle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British expression meaning that's all there is to it, no trouble.

clue.text: Call from Jacob broadcast regularly

indicators.note: regularly picks every third letter of broadcast, starting with its first

explanation.surface: A sound from Jacob is transmitted at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob here is a breed of sheep, not the biblical patriarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jacob is a breed of sheep, and a bleat is a sheep's call.

clue.text: Turn with extremely giddy speed

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme letters, first and last, of giddy

parts.note: a rate is a speed

explanation.surface: A spin at dizzying speed.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to turn or rotate around a centre.

clue.text: Half-back a bit short, but one good at clearing

parts.note: demi- is a prefix meaning half

indicators.note: a bit short means the word for back loses its last letter

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A football half-back who is a little small is a fine defensive clearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-back' is a football position in the surface but splits into two pieces here; 'a bit short' drops the last letter of the ship's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A demister clears mist or condensation from a windscreen.
